extraction.decision: accept the refusal; teach the extractor when the pin moves
extraction.rationale: The extractor will not run against v2.3.5: its PrintConfig sanity check expects 744 active literal registrations and finds 749. That is the check working, not failing — it exists to refuse a structural change rather than extract through one. The five extra registrations are named settings, not a parse artefact: filament_colour_mode, filament_is_high_temperature, filament_multi_colors, filament_tower_ironing_area, wipe_tower_wall_gap, with none removed. Consequence, recorded plainly: the leaf-level inventory at v2.3.5 is unknown rather than unchanged, and this report says so instead of printing zeroes. Raising the constant is part of a deliberate bump, never a way to make this audit quiet.

source:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp.decision: five new settings; adopt with the pin, not before
source:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp.rationale: +42/-9. Five settings added, none removed or renamed: filament_colour_mode, filament_is_high_temperature, filament_multi_colors (the v2.3.5 filament colour-sync data model, backing a new src/slic3r/GUI/filamentsync/ subsystem of sixteen files), plus filament_tower_ironing_area and wipe_tower_wall_gap (wipe-tower tuning). This is the one delta that would grow the 789-definition inventory. None is required by an existing OrcaXR workflow, and adopting settings ahead of the engine that honours them would put five controls in the UI that the pinned WASM build ignores — a false success, which the plan forbids.

source:src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp.rationale: The file changed, but +256/-89 is desktop-application bootstrap: bundled flutter_web resource copying with deferred failure reporting, version logging, and Win32 device-notification registration. The parity signal this file feeds is untouched: zero file-wildcard or extension lines touched, so all 16 format filters it feeds are unchanged. The added concerns have no web analogue at all — OrcaXR ships no bundled desktop resource tree.

source:src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.hpp.rationale: The file changed, but +11/-0 declares only the new flutter_web copy helpers and their status enum. The parity signal this file feeds is untouched: no inventory leaf cites this header — it is read for context and feeds nothing — so the change cannot move a leaf.

source:src/slic3r/GUI/MainFrame.cpp.rationale: The file changed, but +38/-13 touches no menu construction at all. The parity signal this file feeds is untouched: zero append_menu_item, append_menu_check_item, append_submenu, AppendSubMenu, AddDropDownSubMenu, or new wxMenuItem lines were added or removed, so all 118 menu actions and 2 device pages it feeds are byte-identical in meaning.

source:src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp.rationale: The file changed, but +1062/-26 is the largest change in the release and none of it is menu construction. The parity signal this file feeds is untouched: zero menu-signal lines touched, so both menu actions it feeds are unchanged; the bulk is the filament colour-sync surface, which reaches parity only through the five new PrintConfig settings dispositioned above.

source:src/slic3r/GUI/PresetComboBoxes.c.rationale: The file changed, but +356/-93 is preset-combo internals and colour-sync wiring. The parity signal this file feeds is untouched: zero menu-signal lines touched, so all 4 menu actions it feeds are unchanged.

source:src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp.decision: two new placements; adopt with the pin, not before
source:src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp.rationale: +51/-15. Exactly two new append_single_option_line calls, for wipe_tower_wall_gap and filament_tower_ironing_area. The other three new settings are not tab-placed at v2.3.5 — they are the colour-sync data model. Tab groups and pages are otherwise unchanged, so the 93 groups and 21 pages this file feeds stand; only the 424 placements would become 426.

target.rationale: v2.3.5 is one release ahead. Its parity-visible surface is five new settings and two new tab placements; everything else it touches in the seventeen extracted files is inert for parity (verified per file below). That is not enough to justify re-pinning mid-plan: a bump reopens every hardware-sensitive item, forces a clean re-apply of the WASM patch set, and invalidates the engine artifact all current evidence was produced against. The pin moves when the plan reaches P12.3, or sooner if a later release touches something that is not inert.
